correctness.rationale: Cayley-Hamilton produces second-order integer recurrence. The map from toral initial state to first two sensor coordinates is finite-to-one surjective because a rational eigenvector would have eigenvalue ±1, incompatible with q≥3, hence pushes Haar to product Haar. Conditional uniform V proves all q³ consecutive triples equiprobable. Conditional 000 coordinate wrap is excluded by 2/q<1; exact threshold f_j=(q/2+j)/(q²-1) gives the complete 000d conditional law and proves a nonzero fourth-block deviation. Direct Fraction-based polygon clipping exhausts q³ triples for q=3,4,5 and 000d for each; checks supplement unrestricted derivation.

value.rationale: The result explains an exact finite-observation independence-depth transition in the canonical family of hyperbolic trace-q toral automorphisms, uniform over every integer coordinate sensor, and explicitly quantifies the fourth-block anomaly. The trace-matched resolution gives a natural mathematical reason for q bins; the fact cannot be inferred from entropy, pairwise correlation, or generic Markov-coding existence alone.
